answer.rationale: The write-path p99 spike began within the window of a release that went out 2 hours ago, matching the pattern in memory_b1 where a rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact. I have no indication of regional degradation (so failover is premature), no indication of a partner dependency failure (so circuit breaker is not indicated), and adding capacity during peak settlement traffic risks destabilizing a system already showing degraded writes. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) addresses read/dashboard load, not write-path latency. A rollback is the fastest, most surgical intervention that directly preserves customer writes: it removes the suspected cause of write-path degradation while the prior build—known stable per memory_b1—absorbs peak settlement traffic. Verification of memory_b1 confirms that rolling back cleared the spike and completed without customer impact, which is exactly the constraint I care about here.
